title: Signed-in reader sends private feedback from a report, and the owner reads it with its sender in that report's admin view
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C1: A signed-in reader can send a private feedback message from a report page (form on /reports/<slug>, a public POST handler that takes it only from a signed-in reader, and storage for it): missing
C2: The feedback box is separate from public comments: its own form and its own write, and a message never appears in the comment thread: missing
C3: Only the author can see feedback messages: not on any reader page, including the sender's own view of the report, and not through any route a non-owner can reach: missing
C4: The owner reads each report's feedback, each message with its sender (GitHub login/avatar), on that report's admin page next to its dislike count: missing

e005-finish-feedback-interface: not measurable on any machine here: Whether the E-005 finish test passes against a built binary [N-059] -- needs first: The one finish test walks the whole E-005 scenario, so it cannot pass until the reply route exists: an adminRoutes row POST /admin/feedback/{n}/reply taking one 'body' field (SC-017). That row has to join the owner access matrix. The send/read half (SC-016) can be built to the assumed interface, but its finish check stays red until SC-017 lands.

Where feedback_replies is created. Practice puts it in 0005 now; crossdomain puts it in a 0006 owned by SC-017. Chosen: 0005, because SC-017 has no design or spike lap. A reviewer who prefers this slice's schema strictly minimal can move it, at the cost of an unpinned two-hop cascade.
The success fragment and confirmation. Practice uses #feedback and no confirmation; crossdomain uses #feedback-sent with a CSS :target 'Sent to the author.' note. Chosen: #feedback.

Method names: ForOwner/Reply/SenderThreads (practice) against OwnerInbox/OwnerReply/OwnerReplyTarget/Mine (crossdomain). Chosen: Owner* for the owner side and SenderThreads for the reader side, because each fence then matches only its own method.
Admin markup: <article id=feedback-n> (practice) against <li id=feedback-n> in an <ol> (crossdomain). Chosen: article. The finish test's parser handles both.
Reply handler order: practice parses the body before the target lookup, crossdomain looks the target up first. Chosen: lookup first.
Whether SenderThreads is read for the owner's own reader page. Chosen: not, because the owner's box shows the admin link.
